correctness.rationale: The height truncation T_b preserves every formula at a world whose remaining path height is at most b; this is proved by simultaneous structural induction, including the dead-end case. Hence any modal operand at a height-h world is equivalent across all successors to a depth-(h−1) operand, allowing the h≤H witness hypothesis to supply full witnesses. For each H≥1 a countable root with deterministic branches of length H−1 has all shallower successor trees identical but carries endpoint truth values 1/n, forcing the depth-H box infimum 0 unattained. Resource corollaries follow from finite successor sets and finite closure of Gödel operations. Exact-rational finite tests through height 6 corroborate evaluations only.

value.rationale: The 2026 witnessed Gödel semantics makes attainment at every modal depth a natural nonlocal semantic requirement. This theorem converts the unbounded modal-depth requirement into a sharp depth-bounded condition on the geometrically natural bounded-height class, with a family demonstrating that no shallower test suffices for any height. The obstruction requires only one truth-valued variable and the minimum branching pathology, delimiting where bounded-depth witness checks and FMP-style model constructions can fail. The result is an exact complete parameterized boundary, not a numerical improvement or restatement of the model-completeness theorem.
